meta.note: No source had published anything carrying today's date when the run started, so the window ends on 6 September. Pieces that already ran in the 4, 5 and 6 September editions are not repeated, which leaves the OpenAI agent incident and the Seattle Times suit out even though both are still in the pool. The UX Collective piece is summarised from title and standfirst only: Cloudflare blocked two fetch attempts, which is a bot check rather than a paywall. arXiv did not respond.

stories.title: AI adoption in product teams turns from scattered to deliberate
stories.blurb: Taken from the summary alone: the argument is that companies are dropping piecemeal AI initiatives in favour of planned adoption, and that the change shows up first in how design, engineering and product hand work to each other.

sources.headline: AI in Product teams: In 2026, the growing impact on collaboration

stories.title: Designers spent nine months on waste facility floors before drawing anything
stories.blurb: Fifteen designers toured sorting plants, an energy-from-waste facility and a furniture remanufacturing hub, then took six weeks on live briefs from Biffa and Decathlon. The outputs are unusually concrete: a toothbrush with a base wide enough not to drop through an industrial sorting trommel, and a platform that tracks material lifecycles between product designers and waste operators.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: CIWM and URGE Collective reveal circular design sprint outcomes tackling industrial waste

stories.title: OpenAI's launch ad sells the design workflow, not the model
stories.blurb: The spot has Astra draw a rocket, model it in Blender, drop it into a game and order dinner along the way, which is what the criticism latches onto. OpenAI's own demo page goes further and pitches Blender-to-Unreal walkthroughs at designers and their clients, citing Playco as having halved manual fixes in prototyping.

sources.headline: OpenAI's controversial ChatGPT-6 Astra advert paints a sad vision of the future

stories.title: Match the material to the subject, then refuse to apply it evenly
stories.blurb: Helen Ahpornsiri builds animals from pressed plants taken from the habitat each animal lives in, so a hedgehog arrives in the browns and ochres of an October woodland floor. The transferable part is the second move: the density of the technique surges and recedes across a picture instead of being spread consistently.

stories.title: UK design is bigger than retail, and most of its value sits outside design firms
stories.blurb: The Design Council puts the design economy at £136.7bn of gross value added for 2023, up 40% since 2019 and 5.5% of UK output. Two-thirds of that, £90.6bn, is generated by designers working inside manufacturing, healthcare, engineering and finance rather than in agencies, and employment in those non-design sectors grew 20% against 6% in the design industries.

sources.name: Design Week
sources.headline: Design sector outpaces retail to become 136.7bn pillar of UK economy

stories.title: Publishers claim shares of the Anthropic payout on rights they gave back years ago
stories.blurb: The settlement pays $3,000 per work, split evenly with a publisher where the publisher still holds rights and paid in full to self-published authors. Authors report claims on titles whose rights reverted long before the August 2022 cutoff, one of them seventeen years earlier, and the Authors Guild reads the pattern as poor record keeping rather than intent.

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement

stories.title: Astra's computer-use numbers, and a mail client redesign that split its users
stories.blurb: On OSWorld 2.0 the model is reported at 72.6% accuracy at roughly 40 minutes per task, against 65.7% at 75 minutes for its predecessor, and it fills existing presentation templates rather than producing generic decks. The same issue covers Superhuman's mobile redesign, which traded interactions power users had built habits around for a faster search.
